notes: Summary: Mid-market SaaS building an embedded conversational assistant for customer success + ops automation.
Workload: Agentic chat that does multi-step flows: user prompt -> KB search -> action (ticket create, run query) -> confirmation to user.

Primary goals: 1) hit median latency <150ms for streaming first token/partial responses; 2) high reliability for tool calls (idempotency, retries, timeouts); 3) predictable cost for bursty nightly workflows.
POC scope: hosted API only initially. Measure: streaming ttf (time-to-first-token), end-to-end tool-call success rate, KV cache hit improvement with prefix caching.

Tech notes from SE (Diego): currently prototyping with streaming + function-calls. Observed a couple of 5-10s tool-call timeouts in internal sim; wants guidance on backoff and fallback model variants.
Quote: Product lead said, 'We need the assistant to take actions reliably — if a tool call fails it must surface clearly and offer safe rollback.'
Security: require SSO (SAML), audit logs for all function calls, KMS integration for customer keys, and EU data residency for parts of customer data.
Commercial: interested in starting hosted POC with potential move to Dedicated for predictable throughput. Pricing sensitivity around per-token vs flat burst allowance; AE to share pricing worksheet.

Open technical questions: how Redwood handles partial stream + tool-call coordination (do you buffer until tool call returns or stream intermediate steps?), recommended timeout defaults, and circuit-breaker behavior for third-party tools.

Action items: SE to run focused test that reproducibly triggers tool-call timeout and capture logs; AE to circulate pricing worksheet and Dedicated sizing template; security to receive SOC2 + encryption annex.
Short-term ask from customer: 'Can we get a reproducible test harness and a patch for better client-side retry semantics?'
